claim: The GRPO policy gradient is mathematically equivalent to the gradient of an AUC-optimization objective using the linear surrogate loss phi(t)=-t and scoring function f=lpm (mean log-probability/perplexity), and this linear surrogate is provably INCONSISTENT for AUC optimization.
stance_target: standard GRPO reward-only advantage estimation is a valid (consistent) surrogate for discriminative calibration (AUC)
scope_conditions: GRPO and reward-only advantage estimators (also shown to extend to GSPO)
quoted_support: Theorem 3. The gradient of the GRPO objective coincides with the gradient of the AUC optimization objective with surrogate loss phi(t)=-t and scoring function f=lpm (i.e., perplexity). This surrogate loss is inconsistent for AUC optimization.

claim: A surrogate loss for AUC pairwise optimization is consistent (converges to optimal AUC as surrogate risk is minimized) if and only if it is a convex, differentiable, non-increasing function phi with phi'(0)<0; logistic and exponential losses satisfy this, but the linear loss phi(t)=-t implicit in GRPO does not.
stance_target: formal AUC-consistency theory (Gao and Zhou 2012) as the load-bearing tool distinguishing consistent from inconsistent discrimination surrogates
scope_conditions: AUC pairwise ranking surrogate loss design
quoted_support: The surrogate loss Psi(f,o_i,o_j) is consistent with AUC if phi: R->R is a convex, differentiable, and non-increasing function with phi'(0)<0.

claim: CAPO replaces GRPO's advantage estimator with one derived from a logistic AUC surrogate phi_tau(t)=log(1+exp(-t/tau)), where t=(lpm(o1)-lpm(o2))(R1-R2); the resulting per-response advantage tilde{A}_i sums sigmoid-weighted pairwise confidence-gap terms against all oppositely-labeled responses in the group.
stance_target: a discrimination-consistent pairwise ranking surrogate (not a proper scoring rule) can replace GRPO's advantage estimator while remaining a single RL objective
scope_conditions: CAPO advantage estimation, per training group of G rollouts
quoted_support: tilde{A}_i = -sum_{j:R_j=0} phi'(lpm_theta(o_i)-lpm_theta(o_j)), R_i=1; sum_{j:R_j=1} phi'(lpm_theta(o_j)-lpm_theta(o_i)), R_i=0, where phi'(t)=-sigma(-t).

claim: CAPO adds a reference-model-based PPL noise-masking term that excludes correct responses with reference-model perplexity above an upper threshold (likely lucky guesses) and incorrect responses with reference-model perplexity below a lower threshold (likely near-correct reasoning penalized as failure), using the base model's own calibration as a free noise filter.
stance_target: outcome-only binary rewards in RLVR introduce label noise at the level of individual samples that destabilizes training unless explicitly filtered
scope_conditions: CAPO training stability mechanism; thresholds set to upper/lower quartiles of reference-model PPL distribution
quoted_support: we exclude correct responses with reference-model PPL exceeding ref-high (likely lucky guesses) and incorrect responses with reference-model PPL below ref-low (likely near-correct reasoning penalized as failure).
numbers: thresholds = upper/lower quartiles of reference-model PPL distribution

claim: On AIME 2025, CAPO increases AUC-mean from 0.63 to 0.78 (~15%) for the 1.5B model and from 0.54 to 0.79 (~25%) for the 7B model relative to GRPO, while matching or exceeding GRPO's mean@8 accuracy; CAPO also achieves the highest inference-time-scaling accuracy on AIME 2024/2025 (e.g. 25.33% vs GRPO's 20.33% for 1.5B, 38.33% vs 33.33% for 7B).
stance_target: a consistent AUC-surrogate advantage estimator jointly improves discrimination and accuracy relative to GRPO
scope_conditions: Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B/7B, AIME 2024/2025 and six math benchmarks total, DeepScaler training data
quoted_support: CAPO increases AUC by approximately 15% for the 1.5B model (from 0.63 to 0.78) and by about 25% for the 7B model (from 0.54 to 0.79).

claim: Absolute calibration metrics (ECE) do not ensure instance-level discrimination -- assigning identical confidence (e.g. 0.5) to both correct and incorrect responses perfectly satisfies absolute calibration yet is useless for ranking -- whereas relative calibration (AUC) explicitly enforces pairwise separability, motivating CAPO's exclusive focus on AUC over ECE.
stance_target: discriminative/relative calibration metrics (AUC/AUROC) are more meaningful for downstream utility than absolute calibration metrics (ECE) alone
scope_conditions: choice of calibration metric for RLVR reasoning models
quoted_support: assigning identical confidence (e.g., 0.5) to both correct and incorrect responses perfectly satisfy absolute calibration criteria yet fails to distinguish them, limiting its usefulness for downstream tasks such as inference-time scaling.

claim: CAPO experiments used Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B and 7B trained via full RL fine-tuning (verl framework) on 8xA100 GPUs, requiring 24 hours (1.5B) or 48 hours (7B) to convergence -- a multi-GPU compute budget, with no LoRA or parameter-efficient variant reported.
stance_target: single-GPU 7B-scale feasibility of AUC-surrogate calibration-aware RL training
quoted_support: Experiments were conducted using the verl framework on 8xA100 GPUs. Training a single CAPO/GRPO run to convergence takes approximately 24 hours for the 1.5B model and 48 hours for the 7B model.

claim: Ablating CAPO's masking mechanism causes model entropy to gradually increase leading to early stagnation or degradation in accuracy, while applying masking alone to plain GRPO fails to improve AUC -- demonstrating that both the consistent AUC surrogate and the noise-masking are jointly necessary.
stance_target: training instability/entropy collapse is a distinct risk from calibration degradation and requires its own mitigation beyond a better discrimination-consistent loss
quoted_support: removing the masking mechanism causes the model entropy to gradually increase, leading to early stagnation or even degradation in accuracy... applying only masking to GRPO fails to improve AUC, demonstrating that a consistent surrogate objective is essential.
